evals.name: consolidate-on-ruff
evals.prompt: Our Python repo runs black, isort, and flake8 through pre-commit, and they keep producing conflicting changes that fight each other. Set up a single modern tool to own formatting and linting, and simplify the configuration.
evals.trap: A weak fix tweaks the existing three tools or adds Ruff alongside black. Ruff replaces all three; running black with ruff format means two formatters fighting again.
expectations: Recommends Ruff as the single tool (ruff format + ruff check)
Removes black, isort, and flake8 (does not keep black alongside ruff format)
Notes ruff format and ruff check are separate commands and both are run

evals.name: pinned-noqa
evals.prompt:
Suppress the linter warning on this single line without disabling unrelated checks on it.

```python
import settings  # flagged as unused, but imported for its import-time side effects
```
evals.trap: A bare `# noqa` silences the line entirely, hiding any future, unrelated violation on it. The suppression must pin the specific rule code and say why.
expectations: Pins the specific rule code (e.g. # noqa: F401), not a bare # noqa
Includes a short reason for the suppression
Does NOT use a bare `# noqa`

evals.name: ruff-config-async-service
evals.prompt: Write a `[tool.ruff]` configuration for a Python 3.13 async FastAPI service. We want import sorting, likely-bug detection, automatic upgrades to modern syntax, and flagging of blocking calls made inside async functions.
evals.trap: A generic config omits target-version (so pyupgrade can't rewrite safely) and, most importantly, the ASYNC rule set that catches blocking calls in coroutines — the one rule that matters most for an async service.
